AT0052.title: Malicious Peripherals
AT0052.description: Malicious peripherals are devices into which malicious software writes malicious code via USB interfaces or other means. When the peripheral is plugged into a computer, the malicious code automatically runs, thereby attacking the computer.

AT0052-001.title: KON-Boot
AT0052-001.description: KON-Boot is a tool that bypasses Windows and macOS login passwords. It boots the system from a USB device and modifies the kernel's login-authentication flow, allowing direct access without entering a password. With physical access to a target device, an attacker can read or copy disk files and plant backdoors without cracking or changing the original password, making it a common choice for local privilege escalation and credential theft during internal network penetration.

AT0052-002.title: USB Killer
AT0052-002.description: USB Killer is a device that injects high-voltage electrical current into a computer via the USB port. Once plugged in, it repeatedly discharges high voltage onto the data lines, instantly burning out hardware components such as the motherboard, CPU, and RAM. It is primarily used to physically destroy devices to destroy digital evidence and break forensic chains, or to launch destructive attacks against critical infrastructure, causing irreversible hardware damage and data loss.

references.title: USBKill - USB Kill devices for pentesting & law-enforcement

AT0052-003.title: BadUSB
AT0052-003.description: BadUSB is a USB device pre-loaded with malicious code. When inserted into a computer, the malicious code executes automatically, enabling attacks such as keystroke injection, data exfiltration, or malware installation.

references.title: BadUSB - On Accessories that Turn Evil - Black Hat USA 2014
